provisions.title: Oregon Consumer Privacy Act: duties of controller; prohibitions

provisions.appliesTo: apply to any person that conducts business in this state, or that provides products or services to residents of this state, and that during a calendar year, controls or processes: (A) The personal data of 100,000 or more consumers

quoteReRead.pageText: (b) Process sensitive data about a consumer without first obtaining the consumer’s consent or, if the controller knows the consumer is a child, without processing the sensitive data in accordance with the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act of 1998, 15 U.S.C. 6501 et seq.

provisions.quote: Reveals a consumer’s racial or ethnic background, national origin, religious beliefs, mental or physical condition or diagnosis, sexual orientation, status as transgender or nonbinary
provisions.appliesTo: The personal data of 25,000 or more consumers, while deriving 25 percent or more of the person’s annual gross revenue from selling personal data.

consumer_health_data.note: Oregon Consumer Privacy Act (2023 c.369, operative July 1, 2024) requires consent to process sensitive data, which includes mental or physical condition or diagnosis. No dedicated consumer health data law was found in ORS chapter 646A.

crossCheck.note: ORS 646A.578(2)(b) requires consent for sensitive data. History 2025 c.251, effective 2026-01-01. ORS 646A.570(18)(a)(A) covers mental or physical condition. No dedicated consumer health data law found in ORS 646A. Dates checked against session laws.

freeCopyCases: One free copy of health information for an individual appealing a denial of Social Security disability benefits, paper or electronic (ORS 192.576). Binds covered entities.
feeRules: ORS 192.563: "No more than $30 for copying 10 or fewer pages of written material, no more than 50 cents per page for pages 11 through 50 and no more than 25 cents for each additional page". Also a $5 bonus if mailed within seven business days, plus postage and summary costs. Per-page cap, not counted.
ORS 192.576(3): a fee under ORS 192.563 may be charged when the request is by someone other than the individual or personal representative, or after one copy has been given.

provisions.title: Disclosure to individual appealing denial of Social Security benefits
provisions.quote: In the case of an individual appealing the denial of Social Security disability benefits, a covered entity shall upon request provide to the individual or the individual’s personal representative, free of charge, one copy of the individual’s health information
provisions.appliesTo: Covered entities. The free copy covers health information created after the alleged onset date and before the administrative hearing.

quoteReRead.pageText: (1) In the case of an individual appealing the denial of Social Security disability benefits, a covered entity shall upon request provide to the individual or the individual’s personal representative, free of charge, one copy of the individual’s health information created after the date that the individual alleged as the onset of disability

provisions.title: Data brokers: requirement to register with Department of Consumer and Business Services
provisions.quote: a data broker may not collect, sell or license brokered personal data within this state unless the data broker first registers with the Department of Consumer and Business Services as provided in subsection (3) of this section.
provisions.appliesTo: A business entity or part of a business entity that collects and sells or licenses brokered personal data to another person. Registration requires only a statement of whether residents may opt out.
